concepts.title: Federalism: Meaning and Key Features
concepts.definition: Federalism is a form of government in which sovereignty is constitutionally divided between a central authority and constituent units, each supreme in its own sphere. Its markers are two constitutionally guaranteed tiers of government, a written division of powers, and courts to arbitrate disputes between the tiers.
concepts.key_idea: Two governments, one constitution, no overlapping sovereignty -- federalism is power shared by design.
concepts.textbook_ref: keps207.txt lines 15-120 (introduction and meaning of federalism, key features, dual polity, division of powers, written constitution, arbitration by courts)
question_patterns: define federalism and list its essential features
in class 11 federalism chapter: how does a federal government differ from a unitary government
what is meant by a dual polity
why does federalism require a written constitution
who settles disputes between the union and the states
give examples of federal countries and unitary countries

solution_steps.explain: A federation has a national government plus provincial or state governments, each constitutionally created.
Powers are enumerated and divided so each tier is supreme within its sphere -- neither can abolish the other.
Independent courts interpret the division and settle intergovernmental disputes.

concepts.title: Federalism in the Indian Constitution: Union, States and Lists
concepts.definition: The Indian Constitution creates a two-tier federation with a strong centre. The seventh schedule splits subjects into the union list, state list and concurrent list; residuary powers rest with the Union; and in emergencies the system bends toward unity, with Parliament empowered to legislate on state subjects.
concepts.key_idea: A federation with a unitary tilt -- three lists, residuary power at the centre, and emergency levers that reshape the balance.
concepts.textbook_ref: keps207.txt lines 120-250 (federalism in the indian constitution, union state and concurrent lists, residuary powers, emergency provisions, strong centre)
question_patterns: explain the division of subjects among the union state and concurrent lists
in class 11 federalism chapter: why is the indian federation described as holding together
who has residuary powers under the indian constitution
how do emergency provisions alter the federal balance
on concurrent list subjects which law prevails in a clash
why is india called a federation with a strong centre

solution_steps.explain: Union list covers defence, currency and foreign affairs; state list covers police, agriculture, public health; concurrent list carries education and forests where both may act.
Any subject left unlisted belongs to the Union -- the centre's safety net.
During national emergency Parliament may legislate on state subjects, converting the federation temporarily toward a unitary working.

concepts.title: Conflict-Resolving Federalism: Language, Autonomy and Asymmetric Provisions
concepts.definition: Indian federalism has survived diversity by adjusting. The linguistic reorganisation of states in 1956 honoured language identities without breaking the union; special provisions under Articles 371 and former Article 370 accommodated particular histories; official bilingual policy and state autonomy demands show federation as continuous negotiation.
concepts.key_idea: Flexibility over rigidity -- redrawing boundaries and granting accommodations kept the union together where rigidity would have split it.
concepts.textbook_ref: keps207.txt lines 250-380 (linguistic states, jvp committee and states reorganisation act 1956, official language compromise, special provisions article 370 and 371, demands for autonomy)
question_patterns: why were states reorganised on linguistic lines in 1956
in class 11 federalism chapter: how did the constitution accommodate special provisions for certain states
how was the official language controversy resolved
what are the demands for greater state autonomy
explain asymmetric federalism with indian examples
did linguistic reorganisation weaken or strengthen indian unity

solution_steps.explain: After the Andhra movement, the States Reorganisation Act of 1956 redrew boundaries mainly on language, absorbing identity into federal design.
Hindi became official language with English retained indefinitely by compromise, defusing anti-Hindi agitations.
Articles like 370 (Jammu and Kashmir, until 2019) and 371 series gave tailored provisions, showing asymmetric accommodation inside one federation.

concepts.title: Centre-State Relations and Instruments of Central Control
concepts.definition: Besides the lists, the centre holds levers that tilt the federation: governors appointed by the centre, the President's rule under Article 356, central grants and finance commission allocations, and all-India services staffing state administrations. Sarkaria and Punchhi commissions urged restraint in using these levers so cooperative federalism can work.
concepts.key_idea: Governors, Article 356, grants and shared services -- the centre's levers, and the case for using them sparingly.
concepts.textbook_ref: keps207.txt lines 380-500 (centre state relations, role of governor, presidents rule article 356, sarkaria commission, finance commission, cooperative federalism)
question_patterns: what instruments give the centre control over the states
in class 11 federalism chapter: what is presidents rule under article 356
what are the recommendations of the sarkaria commission on centre state relations
how does the role of the governor create federal friction
how do finance commission grants affect centre state balance
explain cooperative federalism with examples

solution_steps.explain: Appointment of governors, emergency powers under 356, reserve legislation in emergencies, and financial dependence on central transfers.
S.R. Bommai's ruling made President's rule judicially reviewable; commissions urged it as a last resort with prior warning.
Councils, commissions and consultation aim to convert hierarchical control into negotiated, cooperative federalism.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A state passes a law on electricity tariffs while Parliament passes another on the same subject, and the two conflict. Which list covers electricity, and whose law prevails?

solution_template.explain: Electricity sits in the concurrent list, so both levels may legislate on it.
On concurrent subjects, a Union law prevails over a state law to the extent of the repugnance.
A state law can survive with presidential assent where the Constitution so provides -- the federal safety valve.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A state government loses its majority and the centre imposes President's rule within hours. Explain the safeguards now placed on such an action after the Bommai judgement.

solution_template.explain: Article 356 lets the centre take over a state when its constitutional machinery fails.
In S.R. Bommai, the Supreme Court made proclamations judicially reviewable and required testing the majority on the floor first.
President's rule is now a last resort -- floor test, parliamentary approval within two months, and possible revocation by courts.
